source: claude-agent-sdk 0.2.181 in-process MCP server path: Query._handle_sdk_mcp_request, SdkMcpBridge, mcp 2.3.0 lowlevel Server, the create_sdk_mcp_server run_tool handler, jsonschema 4.26.0 with referencing 0.37. Answers use the OK / ERR / RPCERR text format of python_schema.json.
assumptions: sys.getrecursionlimit() is the default 1000 and CPython 3.12 counts every Python frame, generator frames included, from the module frame (depth 1); a RecursionError is raised when a push would exceed 1000.

The event loop is started by asyncio.run called directly from module level, so run_tool sits at absolute frame depth 16 and jsonschema.validate at depth 17 on this path. Each extra caller frame under the event loop lowers the budget by one; a boundary moves by one nesting level each time the lost frames cross the per-level cost of that shape.

answers is the steady state: each case ran in a fresh process after its warmup call (the same shape at depth 1, on its own server) completed, then the case was sent twice on one server with identical answers.

cold_answers is present only where the case sent alone in a fresh process answers differently. The cause is the collections.abc and numbers ABC caches: the first isinstance check of a type against an ABC walks __instancecheck__ and __subclasscheck__ frames; if that first walk overflows, the negative cache is never filled and the cold answer repeats on every later call in that process.
depth is the nesting count N given to the shape builder, not a frame count. last_ok and first_rec are N and N+1 at the boundary; infinite cases have no depth.

A RecursionError caught by run_tool surfaces as its text. When str() of a SchemaError overflows inside run_tool's exception handler, the exception leaves the handler and the mcp server answers with JSON-RPC error code 0, shown as RPCERR.

depth is the number of nested groups (or lookaheads, or conditionals) in the pattern. The pattern is compiled first by check_schema, through the format checker of the regex format on pattern and on propertyNames of patternProperties (drafts 6 and later), and again by validation (pattern, the patternProperties keys, and the joined additionalProperties pattern). re caches only patterns that compiled, so the deepest compile of a pattern decides the boundary.
Each warmup uses a different pattern from its case, so the case pattern is never in the re cache when the case starts.

The regex cache cases (named regex cache) keep a pattern of 60 nested groups whose first compile is check_schema's, on the pattern under $defs, which the core vocabulary checks before allOf. allOf then holds the filler patterns of the layout (distinct one-character-class patterns) with the same pattern again between each count, checked in array order. re keeps compiled patterns in _cache2 (first in first out, 256) and _cache (least recently used, 512); a pattern found only in _cache moves to its end and joins _cache2, and one found in _cache2 moves nowhere. The instance nests depth levels under root, and the search of the pattern at the deepest level overflows only when the pattern left both caches.
